abstract: In cereal roots the metaxylem vessels are the main channels of axial water transport. Metaxylem size and number are considered constant traits characterising different root classes. Here we show that metaxylem number is progressively remodelled along root axes, producing mature roots with vascular anatomy differing by position. At initiation, adventitious wheat root tips produce multiple files of metaxylem, and then progressively fewer, until a single central metaxylem file exists, resembling the vascular anatomy of the seminal roots. This pattern was observed in wheat, barley, rye, oat, and Brachypodium, but not in maize or sorghum. We investigated the developmental regulation of this phenomenon by creating a cell-resolved spatial transcriptomic atlas of wheat adventitious root tips in these different metaxylem production states and integrated this with bulk RNA-seq analysis of whole root tips. We developed a pipeline integrating these complementary transcriptomic datasets to reveal differentially expressed genes that included candidates controlling meristem maintenance, vascular patterning, and metaxylem wall lignification. Hydraulic modelling revealed changes in vessel number reduces pressure in vasculature, while maintaining or increasing the capacity of roots to transport water. We propose that this developmental transition preconfigures different regions of the root for their changing hydraulic environments, providing a mechanism to balance hydraulic robustness and efficiency over the root life cycle.
